findings.reason: LlvmIr.targets:277 swaps in any prelink/<name>.dll that exists, without checking that this run wrote it. PreTrimmingFixLegacyDesigner.cs only creates the directory and writes a file when ProcessAssemblyDesigner returns true; it never deletes anything. When a library is upgraded to a version with no legacy designer, ProcessAssemblyDesigner returns false ('has no designer' or 'already processed', FixLegacyResourceDesignerStep.cs:72-80), so the old v1 copy is still swapped in and shipped.
findings.claim: Stale prelink copies are never cleared, so a library that no longer needs rewriting is still replaced by an old rewritten copy from an earlier build.
findings.evidence: The swap target picks any ResolvedFileToPublish .dll for which `Exists('$(IntermediateOutputPath)prelink/%(Filename)%(Extension)')` is true and points it at that file. It does not check whether the current run produced the file. PreTrimmingFixLegacyDesigner.RunTask only calls `Directory.CreateDirectory (OutputDirectory)` (PreTrimmingFixLegacyDesigner.cs:46) and writes a file only when `ProcessAssemblyDesigner` returns true. It never deletes anything. The `<FileWrites>` entry is added in the inner per-RID build, where IncrementalClean is deliberately removed (AssemblyResolution.targets:23-26), so nothing else cleans the directory. Trigger: build once with library X v1, which has a legacy Resource class; prelink/X.dll is written. Then upgrade X to v2, built with the designer assembly. The task reruns because its inputs are newer, but FixLegacyResourceDesignerStep.ProcessAssemblyDesigner returns false for v2 ("has already been processed" / "has no designer"), so nothing is written. Exists() still finds the v1 prelink copy, so ResolvedFileToPublish is pointed at the old v1 code before ILLink runs.

findings.reason: The target's Outputs is only _PreTrimmingFixLegacyDesigner.stamp; the prelink files are not listed. MSBuild skips the target when every input is older than the stamp, which happens when a NuGet library whose dll keeps an old pack timestamp is added. The diff also removed the post-trim FixLegacyResourceDesignerStep, so nothing else rewrites that library.
findings.claim: The rewrite target's up-to-date check uses only a stamp file, so a newly added assembly that is older than the stamp, or a deleted prelink directory, skips the rewrite with no error.
findings.evidence: `Inputs="@(_PreTrimmingAssembly)" Outputs="$(_AndroidStampDirectory)_PreTrimmingFixLegacyDesigner.stamp"`. The prelink files are not listed as outputs. The update target only swaps files that `Exists()`, so when prelink/ is missing while the stamp is current, nothing is rewritten and nothing is swapped. In that case nothing fixes the library: this change removed the post-trimming FixLegacyResourceDesignerStep from PostTrimmingPipeline and removed the designer TrimmerRootDescriptor. The unrewritten library keeps reading its own Resource fields, which hold the IDs from its own compile. Elsewhere this repo tracks item-set changes with hash files (e.g. `_ResolvedUserAssembliesHashFile` in AssemblyResolution.targets); this target has no such check.

members.claim: The rewrite target counts as up to date based on a single stamp file. If the prelink copies are deleted, or an assembly is added whose timestamp is older than the stamp, the target is skipped and legacy libraries go to ILLink without being rewritten, with no error at build time.

findings.reason: _PreTrimmingFixLegacyDesignerUpdateItems is defined only in TypeMap.LlvmIr.targets. Xamarin.Android.Common.targets:2880-2881 imports that file only when _AndroidTypeMapImplementation != 'trimmable', and TypeMap.Trimmable.targets:30-31 accepts NativeAOT. NativeAOT.targets:270 depends on that target unconditionally. Kept at medium because the trimmable path is experimental.
findings.claim: With NativeAOT and the trimmable typemap, _AndroidRunNativeCompile depends on a target that is never defined, so the build fails with MSB4057.
findings.evidence: `DependsOnTargets="_PreTrimmingFixLegacyDesignerUpdateItems;NativeCompile"`. That target is defined only in Microsoft.Android.Sdk.TypeMap.LlvmIr.targets. Xamarin.Android.Common.targets:2880-2881 imports that file only when `'$(_AndroidTypeMapImplementation)' != 'trimmable'`. The trimmable path is a supported NativeAOT combination: TypeMap.Trimmable.targets:9 imports TypeMap.Trimmable.NativeAOT.targets, and `_ValidateTrimmableTypeMapRuntime` accepts NativeAOT. NativeAOT.targets is always imported for `_AndroidRuntime=NativeAOT` (Microsoft.Android.Sdk.targets:36), and a missing target in DependsOnTargets is a hard error. This path is experimental, which is why this is medium.

findings.reason: FixLegacyResourceDesignerStep.ProcessAssembly:63 does skip IsMainAssembly, so the comment's main-assembly claim holds. ProcessAssemblyDesigner (lines 69-105) only rewrites ldsfld against the assembly's own legacy designer, so processing the main assembly never fixed its references into another library's Resource class. The described breakage is not caused by this change.
findings.claim: The new task skips the main assembly, unlike the removed post-trim wrapper, and its comment claims a filter match.
findings.evidence: The comment says "Match the filtering in FixLegacyResourceDesignerStep.ProcessAssembly", followed by `if (Path.GetFileNameWithoutExtension (item.ItemSpec) == TargetName) continue;` and an IsFrameworkAssembly skip. ProcessAssembly actually filters on `context.IsMainAssembly || !context.IsAndroidUserAssembly`, so the two filters differ. The removed PostTrimmingFixLegacyResourceDesignerStep doc said it called ProcessAssemblyDesigner directly, "matching the behavior of the former ILLink path which processed all assemblies without StepContext flag filtering". The rewritten libraries get `ClearDesignerClass (designer, completely: true)`, which empties NestedTypes, so an `ldsfld Lib.Resource/Layout::X` in the skipped main assembly can no longer resolve.
